senses.gloss: to divide, tear. Ab. d’R. N., 2ⁿᵈ vers., ch. XLIII (ed. Schechter, p. 122) שחץ שהוא שׁוֹחֵץ בפיו the lion is called shaḥats, because he tears with his mouth; Yalk. Prov. 959 שהוא מְשַׁחֵץ בשיניו (Pi.).—2) to divide off, separate.—Part. pass. שָׁחוּץ; pl. שְׁחוּצִים, שְׁחוּצִין

units: <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 6:1:11">Y. Sabb. <cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 4:8:3">Cant. R. to IV, 8</cite> (ref. to <he>אריות</he> <cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 4:8:3">ib.</cite>) <he>מה הארי הזה ש׳ … ש׳ וגבורים וכ׳</he> (strike out <he>וגבורים</he>) as the lion is proud (keeping for himself), so were Sihon and Og proud (selfish) … they did not come to each other’s rescue; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 988:40">Yalk. ib. 988</cite> <he>מה הארי הזה שחק</he> (corr. acc.).—

senses.gloss: to separate one’s self, be exclusive, lofty.
units: Sifré Num. 131 מלכות זו מתגאה ומִשְׁתַּחַצַת וכ׳ this proud and overweening government has only four provinces worthy of an empire &c.; Yalk. Num. 771; Yalk. Deut. 809. Ab. d’R. N. l. c. [read:] שחץ שהוא מִשְׁתַּחֵץ the lion is called shaḥats, because he is proud.
